2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 Smt. Syeda Fajilath Fathima and accused No.1 was solemnized on 01-10-2021 as per the Muslim customs and rites.

After the marriage, they were living in the house No.1/1, 4th Floor, Penta House, 2nd Cross, Rahamathnagara within the limits of R.T.Nagara PS, at that time the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention started harassing CW1 mental and physical cruelty by stating that at the time of marriage the parents of CW1 did not gave any dowry and hence they demanded her to bring Car, Rs.20 lakhs and gold necklace, earrings, ring as a dowry from her parental house by abusing and thrown her out of house.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt.Syeda Fajilath Fathima CW7 Smt Choodamani ASI of R.T.Nagara Police Station registered a Crime No.167/2023 against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) R/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 3, 4 of D.P. Act, prepared FIR and KABC030372012023 CC No.21379/2023 sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.

4. Investigation: After registration of FIR, CW8 Sri Shivakumar drawn spot mahazar on 04-06-2023 as per Ex.P2 and continued the investigation, collected the documents, recorded the statement of R T Nagar Police Station vs Syed Yaseen Ahmed on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102402112/
2 witnesses and submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) R/w Section 34 of IPC and Section 3, 4 of D.P.Act.
5.

6. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused No.1 to 4.
7.
Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused No.1 to 4, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A) read with sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act has been framed, read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 4 in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Prosecution Evidence: The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 8 witnesses, examined one witness and exhibited two documents.

The learned Sr.APP prayed for issuance of summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as CW1 obtained the divorce from accused No.1 and hence the examination of CW2 to CW8 has been dispensed with by the order dated 09-10-2024.

9. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused persons from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused persons as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
10. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

11. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW1 Smt.
Syeda Fajilath Fathima and accused No.1 was solemnized on 01-10-2021 as KABC030372012023 CC No.21379/2023 per the Muslim customs and rites and they were living in the house No.1/1, 4th Floor, Penta House, 2nd Cross, Rahamathnagara within the limits of R.T.Nagara PS, at that time the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention started harassing CW1 with mental and physical cruelty to bring Car, Rs.20 lakhs and gold necklace, earrings, ring as a dowry from her parental house and thrown her out of the house thereby subjected her to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable u/Sec.498(A) R/w sec.34 of IPC and u/Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
2. What order?
12. The court's findings on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative  Point No.2 : As per final order R T Nagar Police Station vs Syed Yaseen Ahmed on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102402112/
3  KABC030372012023 CC No.21379/2023  REASONS 13. Point No.1: In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 11 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows i. CW1 by name Smt. Syed Fajilath Fathima, being Informant examined as PW1 and deposed that she has identified Ex.P1 complaint and Ex.P2 spot mahazar and her signatures thereon as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a).

sentences.text: She further stated that when she went to police station for settlement of minor differences of opinion amongst her and accused No.1, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and 2.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.
14. PW1 is the informant cum victim has not supported the prosecution case.

Though the prosecution has cross examined her by treating as hostile witness, no favorable answers has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case that she has deposed falsely to help the accused.

Thus, it emerges from the deposition of PW1 that the disputes between the accused and the PW1 have been settled.

But the learned Sr.APP argued that the Section 498(A) of Indian Penal Code is not compoundable case as per section 320 of CR.P.C. and hence the examination of witnesses is R T Nagar Police Station vs Syed Yaseen Ahmed on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102402112/
4 necessary but this court dispensed the same on account of amicable settlement arrived between the rival parties to the case.

sentences.text:
This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR IN THE MATTER OF AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.
15.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This court further places reliance upon the decision in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
KABC030372012023 CC No.21379/2023 "It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
16. ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.

The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case KABC030372012023 CC No.21379/2023 and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar)
2014 4 464, wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
18.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
In this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the alleged offences cannot be proved beyond R T Nagar Police Station vs Syed Yaseen Ahmed on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102402112/
5 reasonable doubt.

ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 4 found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A) read with section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
